idiom_name: staged POSIX access: open plus pread for the cheap part, mmap window for the expensive part
implementation_notes: C gives every stage its own primitive but no composition: open() returns a cheap descriptor for the whole resource, pread() reads the small self-describing part (header, index, table of contents) without disturbing a shared file offset, and the expensive part is mapped with mmap() so that the kernel supplies pages only as they are touched. The same shape covers code as a resource: dlopen(path, RTLD_LAZY) loads the shared object and resolves function symbols only when referencing code first executes, so an optional feature that is never called never pays for that part. Because C has neither destructors nor resource types, the plan and the reverse-order release (munmap before close, dlclose for the object) must be written at every call site or hidden behind a small staged struct with a matching release function; the classic hand-written form is therefore justified whenever the resource does not fit in memory or when the provider must not be touched beyond its first part.
code_sketch:
int fd = open("pack.bin", O_RDONLY);              /* stage 1: cheap descriptor */
struct idx ix; pread(fd, &ix, sizeof ix, 0);      /* stage 1: header, unshared  */
void *part = mmap(NULL, ix.len, PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE, fd, ix.off);
if (part == MAP_FAILED) { close(fd); return -1; } /* stage 2: mapping created */
consume(part, ix.len);        /* pages faulted in only as they are touched */
munmap(part, ix.len); close(fd);                  /* staged release, reverse    */
pitfalls: Short reads: read()/pread() may return fewer bytes than requested, so a stage that assumes a full transfer silently produces a truncated part; loop until the stage size is reached and treat a premature 0 as end-of-resource.

A mapping is not a snapshot: if the file is truncated or replaced while the window is mapped the access fault is SIGBUS rather than an errno, so partial mapping requires a provider guaranteed stable for the lifetime of the window.

Nothing releases for you: address space (munmap) and descriptor (close) are separate stages and both must run on every exit path, including the error path where the mapping succeeded but the caller gave up.

dlopen with RTLD_LAZY defers function-symbol resolution only - the manual notes that references to variables are always bound immediately - so a plugin relying on lazy binding of globals can still fail at load time.

variants.name: dlopen with RTLD_LAZY symbol binding
variants.idiom_name: dlopen(path, RTLD_LAZY) plus dlsym per symbol
variants.implementation_notes: The stages are load and resolve: dlopen() returns a handle to the shared object while function symbols are resolved only as the code that references them executes, so a program can offer optional subsystems and pay for each only when it is used. dlsym() is the second stage per symbol; dlclose() (or RTLD_NODELETE when the object must stay mapped) releases the stage. Keep the resolved function pointers in a small struct filled on first use so the binding policy stays in one place; use RTLD_NOW instead when a missing symbol must be a load-time failure rather than a first-use one.
pitfalls: RTLD_LAZY defers only function symbols; data symbols are bound when the object is loaded, so a plugin that reads globals at load time can still fail immediately.
Dangling function pointers: the resolved symbols become invalid once dlclose() drops the reference count, so the caller must not keep them beyond the handle lifetime.
RTLD_NODELETE and reference counts interact: reopening the same object returns the same handle (documented), so a stage that believes it loaded a private copy may share state with another component.
